name: thinking-tools
description: Thinking-tool skills for harder, more honest AI assistance: board (adversarial multi-expert critique), premortem (name what could go wrong before committing to a plan), but-for-real (no success claims without actually running the thing), self-rate (grade your own draft before the user does), code-simplifier (clarity-preserving refactors of recent changes), weekly-automation-review (spot repetitive work worth automating — reads the cross-repo prompt log, per-repo memory indexes and the Stop hooks' acted-on rates and the skill-candidate queue when the dev-hooks plugin is installed), retro (/retro flags a session that went badly; the prompt log records it for that review to diagnose), commit-digest (pull applicable improvements from tracked external repos, feeds and pages), adr (record significant architectural decisions with context, reasoning, and consequences), grill (relentless one-question-at-a-time interview until a plan is fully specified), domain-modeling (build and sharpen a CONTEXT.md ubiquitous-language glossary), codebase-design (deep-modules vocabulary for designing interfaces, seams, and testability), wait-what (re-pitch an answer the person didn't follow, in plain words), brief-back (play a delegated task back as a contract sized to it — depth with a check-in point, done when, what the agent needs — and end with a status), and thinking-toolbox (flag and guide through Adam Jones's 38 thinking tools for choosing, deciding, executing and compounding). Ships a thinking-tools-reminder (SessionStart) hook that nudges Claude to reach for these tools proactively rather than only when asked.
